title: Route parameters
summary: Capture changing parts of a URL, such as a user id, with :name and read them from req.params.

quiz.q: A route is written as `/users/:id`. Which request URL does it match?
quiz.explain: `:id` matches exactly one piece of the path, so `/users/7` matches. `/users` has no second piece and `/users/7/posts` has an extra one.

quiz.q: A browser asks for `/greet/Meena`. What does the server send?
quiz.explain: Express stores the matched piece in `req.params.name`, so the text is `Hi Meena`.

quiz.q: For the URL `/users/42`, what is the type of `req.params.id`?
quiz.explain: Everything in a URL is text. `req.params.id` is the string "42". Use `Number(req.params.id)` when you need a number, for example to compare with `user.id`.

quiz.q: Complete the route so it reads both parameters.
quiz.explain: All named parts of the path live on `req.params`.

quiz.q: Click the line that stops this route from finding the user.
quiz.explain: `u.id` is the number 1 but `req.params.id` is the string "1", and `===` never treats them as equal. Convert first with `Number(req.params.id)`.

exercise.task:
Add three GET routes in `app.js`:

- `/greet/:name` sends the text `Hello, NAME!` (for `/greet/Asha` it sends `Hello, Asha!`).
- `/users/:id` sends the matching user from the `users` array as JSON with `res.json`.
- `/courses/:course/lessons/:lesson` sends the text `Course COURSE, lesson LESSON`, for example `Course html, lesson 3`.

Leave `module.exports = app;` at the bottom.
hints: Put a colon before the changing part of the path, for example `'/greet/:name'`, and read it from `req.params`.
For the user route, find the user with `users.find(...)`. The id in the URL is a string, so use `Number(req.params.id)` before comparing.
